members.name: Tapentadol
members.iupac: Phenol, 3-[(1R,2R)-3-(dimethylamino)-1-ethyl-2-methylpropyl]- (CAS index name, NIST); the hydrochloride as 3-[(1R,2R)-3-(dimethylamino)-1-ethyl-2-methylpropyl]phenol hydrochloride (Federal Register, 2009)
synonyms: NUCYNTA, NUCYNTA ER (tapentadol hydrochloride products, DailyMed)
members.note: DEA drug code 9780 (Federal Register, 2009). The DailyMed label's description section, which gives the salt's formula, could not be read through WebFetch (the text was cut off).

forms.detail: DEA fact sheet: oral solutions, immediate-release and extended-release tablets and capsules, and injectable preparations.

DEA Diversion Control Division (September 2026): tablets, capsules and liquids in a range of colours, markings and packaging; single-ingredient extended-release (OxyContin, Xtampza ER) and immediate-release (Roxicodone, RoxyBond) products; combinations with aspirin (Percodan) or acetaminophen (Percocet, Oxycet).

DEA Diversion Control Division (August 2025): several hundred brand-name and generic products, most of them combinations, hydrocodone with acetaminophen being the combination most often prescribed; on the illicit market, tablets, capsules and liquids, with acetaminophen-containing tablets the form most often encountered.
WHO ATC: codeine as a cough suppressant (R05DA04) and in analgesic combinations without psycholeptics (N02AA59) and with psycholeptics (N02AA79).
DEA Diversion Control Division (May 2026): tablets (generic Ultram), extended-release tablets (generic Ultram ER), capsules (Conzip) and tablets combined with acetaminophen (generic Ultracet).
DailyMed: NUCYNTA (tapentadol hydrochloride) round, biconvex, film-coated tablets in yellow, yellow-orange and orange, marked 'O-M'; NUCYNTA ER film-coated extended-release tablets are also listed.
